clue.text: Little pet's mate turned tail

indicators.note: turned tells us the word for a mate is flipped round to run the other way

parts.note: a pal is a mate
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: A small pet's companion ran away in fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' is the reversal signal; 'tail' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in following a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a small pampered dog kept as a companion animal.

clue.text: Like deposit on bottle everyone used originally

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first pieces above the bottle word

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word used

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A remark about sediment left on a bottle that everybody once used.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'on' means sitting above: the first two pieces stack on top of the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Alluvial describes silt and sand laid down by rivers, a kind of sediment deposit.

clue.text: Verbal onslaught awful people uttered

indicators.note: uttered means the phrase is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like it

parts.note: dire means awful and a tribe is a people, giving dire tribe

explanation.surface: A tirade delivered by some dreadful folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'dire tribe' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter spoken or written attack, a tirade.

clue.text: Argue foolishly about stake bringing security

indicators.note: about tells us the jumbled letters go round the stake
foolishly suggests the letters of argue are jumbled in a silly way

parts.note: the ante is the stake put into the pot at poker

explanation.surface: Quarrelling stupidly over a bet doesn't make anyone feel safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' scrambles the five letters of 'Argue', and 'about' wraps that jumble round the poker stake.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a pledge or surety that gives protection against loss.

clue.text: Suggested a theologian must accept leading position with church

indicators.note: must accept says the theologian takes the following pieces inside

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
the van is the front or leading position, as in vanguard
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar is told to take a prominent role alongside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must accept' means the doubled-letter degree opens up to hold the front position and church together.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced as a verb means put forward or proposed, like an idea offered for consideration.

clue.text: When there's a lowering of cover that may be felt immediately?

definitions.text: When there's a lowering of cover that may be felt
definitions.meaning: read literally: the moment a hat, which may be made of felt, is dropped
the idiom means without hesitation or at once

explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' looks like the verb of sensing but is the hat fabric; dropping a hat was once a signal to start.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a hat dropped as a starting signal, so it means without any delay.

clue.text: Former pupil identifying medicinal compound before dawn?

indicators.note: before puts the compound ahead of the sunrise piece

parts.note: alum is an astringent compound used in medicine
dawn is when the sun comes up; in a down answer the word sun written upwards reads NUS

explanation.surface: An old schoolboy recognising a remedy just before sunrise.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'dawn' is read as 'sun up', which in a down answer means SUN written bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An alumnus is a graduate or past student of a school or college.

clue.text: Councillor formerly brought in to work for musicians

indicators.note: brought in says one piece is placed inside the councillor abbreviation

parts.note: once means formerly, at an earlier time

explanation.surface: An ex-councillor is recruited to perform alongside an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' means the word for formerly goes inside the councillor's abbreviation; 'to' stays as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a composition for a solo instrument with orchestra, a piece written for players.

clue.text: Absolutely secure standoff

parts.note: dead can mean absolutely, as in dead certain
to lock is to make secure

explanation.surface: Something totally safe and firmly fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a situation where neither side can make progress, an impasse.

clue.text: Some of Shaw's plays were so enjoyable, others not

definitions.text: Some of Shaw's plays were so enjoyable, others not

parts.words: Some of Shaw's plays were so enjoyable, others not
parts.note: George Bernard Shaw published his Plays ... and Plays ..., so some were agreeable and others the opposite

explanation.surface: A theatre critic's verdict that Shaw's output was uneven.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw grouped early works as 'Plays Pleasant' and 'Plays Unpleasant'; the answer is also a plain synonym for enjoyable.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means agreeable or enjoyable, and was Shaw's own title for one volume of plays.

clue.text: It'S a republic, sovereign being relatively undervalued

definitions.meaning: a West African republic with Conakry as its capital
an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings, against which the 20-shilling sovereign looks cheap

explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is a British gold coin worth a pound (20 shillings); the coin wanted was worth 21 shillings, so the sovereign is relatively undervalued beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both an African state and an old British coin worth a pound and a shilling.

clue.text: Unexpectedly come upon extra profits

parts.note: over means extra or left over
the take is the takings or profits

explanation.surface: Stumbling on some surprise extra earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overtaken by events is to be caught suddenly by them, as by a storm.

clue.text: Fake a French coin once used in Spain

parts.note: un is the French for a
the real was an old Spanish silver coin

explanation.surface: A counterfeit of an old Spanish coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unreal is not genuine, imaginary or false.

clue.text: Reinforce lock on bar

indicators.note: on places the lock right after the bar piece in this across answer

parts.note: but can mean except, like bar in all bar one
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Strengthen a door by fitting a lock on a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' and 'lock' look like door hardware; they are 'except' and a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttress something is to support or strengthen it, as a wall prop does.

clue.text: Small current — less than amp on line, in a way

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened amp and the line go inside the way

parts.note: a street is a way or road

indicators.note: less than says the word amp loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An electrician's note about a feeble current flowing along a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' drops the final letter of 'amp'; 'in' puts that and the line inside the road word. 'current' and 'amp' suggest electricity, but it is water.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamlet is a little brook, a small stream of flowing water.

clue.text: Fruit for the fleet? Not by the sound of it!

indicators.note: by the sound of it says we want a word that is said the same as another

parts.note: fleet means fast, so not fleet means slow

explanation.surface: A pun on whether some fruit is suitable for a navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' looks like a navy but is the adjective 'fast'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloe is the small dark berry of the blackthorn, used in sloe gin.

clue.text: Hollow glasses filled with something promising

indicators.note: filled with says the glasses hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
an IOU is a written promise to repay a debt

explanation.surface: Empty spectacles holding out some hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filled with' puts the debtor's note inside the spectacles word, before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious means superficially plausible but actually empty or false.

clue.text: "Ring" director who works in the theatre?

definitions.meaning: someone at a telephone exchange who puts calls through
a surgeon, who works in an operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests Wagner and 'theatre' the stage, but they are a phone call and a hospital's operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a switchboard worker and a surgeon who performs operations.

clue.text: Prepare to fire a chum

definitions.meaning: to raise the hammer of a gun ready for shooting
an old British form of address for a male friend

explanation.walkthrough: As a term of address, the second sense is British slang for a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both setting a gun's hammer ready and a friend or pal.

clue.text: Travel north about a mile to get to plant

indicators.note: about says the travel and north pieces go round the next pieces

parts.note: to cycle is to travel by bike

explanation.surface: Ride your bike north for about a mile to reach a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AM inside CYCLEN, between CYCL and EN. 'about' looks like 'roughly' but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The cyclamen is a flowering plant of the primrose family with upswept petals.

clue.text: Ride across island and get shot

indicators.note: across says the ride stretches over and around the island piece

parts.note: a canter is a ride at a gentle gallop

explanation.surface: Gallop over an island and be fired upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a verb but is the ammunition: canister shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Canister is a kind of shot, a case of small balls fired from a cannon.

clue.text: New start for big cat facing unknown danger

indicators.note: new start for says the big cat's first letter is replaced

parts.note: a leopard is a big cat
Y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A big cat makes a fresh start despite facing unknown peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New start for' swaps the L of LEOPARD for J; 'facing' joins on Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy means peril or risk of loss or harm.

clue.text: One who tries frozen stuff and nothing else?

parts.note: just means only, with nothing else
ice is frozen water

explanation.surface: Someone who samples ice and nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tries' suggests tasting, but it is trying cases in court; 'just ice' is frozen stuff only.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice is a judge, who tries cases in court.

clue.text: Fondling worries head of school

parts.note: cares are worries

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of the word school

explanation.surface: A head teacher frets over improper touching at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives S, the first letter of 'school'.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle stroke or fondling touch.

clue.text: Real fun I badly miss in Germany

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of the phrase are put in a poor order

explanation.surface: Missing the real fun in Germany terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a verb of longing but is the title for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fräulein is the German title for an unmarried young woman, equivalent to Miss.

clue.text: Get volunteers to fill old container

indicators.note: to fill says the volunteers go inside the old container

parts.note: a bin is a container
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Recruit volunteers to load an ancient receptacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fill' puts TA inside OBIN. The TA is the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain is to get or acquire.

clue.text: Partner's partial yet ample hand-out rejected

indicators.note: rejected says that run of letters is turned back to front
partial says only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A partner's half-hearted, if generous, handout is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial' picks ETAMPLEH from 'yet ample hand-out'; 'rejected' turns it round. The 's of 'Partner's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmate is a helpful companion, especially a spouse.

clue.text: Sound artist — one superior to Constable?

indicators.note: Sound tells us a word is said aloud to give another

parts.note: John Singer Sargent was a portrait painter

explanation.surface: A painter is said to outrank Constable.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like the English landscape painter, linking with 'artist', but is a police constable; a sergeant ranks above one.
explanation.definitionFit: In the police a sergeant is the rank immediately above constable.

clue.text: Fish with doctor in Arctic waste

indicators.note: in says the doctor is put inside the fish

parts.note: tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish and a doctor out in the frozen north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the doctor's abbreviation inside the fish, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast treeless frozen plain of the Arctic regions.
